newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Saturday on low supply and are likely to rise further amid rumours of damage to crop by pest attack, dealers said.

"Reports of White Fly attack has puzzled spinners as there are no figures available for the extent of damage it has caused," dealer Adil Nasim said. But the rumours of crop damage will push the rates higher, he added.
"According to our estimate losses would not be more than 10 percent of 12 million bales (375 lbs each) expected this year," Nasim said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety from the new 1996/97 crop was traded at 2,200 rupees ($59.36) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
